newsitem.title: UK: LME to strive to keep non-cash clearing - CEO.
newsitem.headline: LME to strive to keep non-cash clearing - CEO.

text.p: The London Metal Exchange (LME) will strive to retain its non-cash clearing system while it is more flexible about its historic price carry mechanism, said David King LME chief executive.
Addressing an LME metals seminar on Monday, he also said that the review of the metals market could continue for some time to come.
Referring to the LME's non-cash clearing system, King said, "We believe we have things well under control."
The non-cash clearing system means that positions on the LME only become payable when the due date becomes prompt.
But on historical price carries, which allow traders to roll over positions at prices other than the prevailing market price, the LME is more flexible.
"We are happy to see what the industry's view is on them (price carries)," King said.
Both of these mechanisms were included in the Securities and Investments Board (SIB) review of the metals markets, prompted by Sumitomo's huge copper losses.
King said the LME was also looking at ways of changing market transparency, although proposals from LME users as to how to improve it were often vague and varied.
"We are working at upgrading our large position reporting system," King said.
He said the review of the metals markets and any changes following the Sumitomo scandal could take considerable time to complete.
"I would not be surprised if the saga was still continuiing this time next year, and potentially a year after that," he said.
King repeated that the LME was limited in what it knew of Sumitomo's unauthorised copper trades.
"There was a huge amount of OTC (Over the Counter) business and physical business about which we knew absolutely nothing."
